messages:
Mia Chen: Heads-up — ran a focused bakeoff comparing FP8-OPT (our fp8 EC4), GPTQ-INT8, and AWQ-INT8 on Llama-70B for the redwood-evals/llmbench-v1 promptset (summaries, code, math).
Mia Chen: Short summary numbers (median across shards):\n- FP8-OPT: throughput 980 tok/s, p95 latency 172ms, eval PPL baseline\n- GPTQ-INT8: throughput 1260 tok/s (+28%), p95 145ms, PPL +0.9\n- AWQ-INT8: throughput 1210 tok/s (+24%), p95 150ms, PPL +0.6 but code-pass@1 -2.1%\nMia Chen: Notable: AWQ had better quality for natural language but degraded on code snippets compared to FP8; GPTQ had higher PPL but slightly better pass@1 on code vs AWQ.
Aj Patel: Nice. Did you run with prefix cache enabled? that tends to change perf/quality balance.
Mia Chen: Yes — runs for each quant variant were done both with prefix/KV cache on and off. Key observation: AWQ-INT8 shows larger latency uplift when prefix cache misses occur (cold start) vs FP8. Continuous batching masks this for steady traffic.
Sam Ortiz: Can you paste the eval command so I can reproduce? also which kernel/runtime flags?
Mia Chen: Sure: \n```bash\n./eval_run.py --model hf/llama-70b --quant awq-int8 --evalset llmbench-v1 \\\n  --batching continuous --prefix-cache enabled --kvcache-size 8GB \\\n  --runtime rtd-1 --threads 4 \\
  --out out/awq-run.json\n```\nRuntime flags: rtd-1 with asm-kernels on, fp8 path used hw-optimized matmul, GPTQ used the gptq-optimized kernels.
Nina Green: Did you capture a per-route token-cost breakdown? curious how cost/unit changes with caching.
Mia Chen: Yes — when prefix cache hit-rate >= 85%: AWQ unit cost ~0.62x FP8. But at hit-rate < 30% (many short unique prompts): AWQ cost ~0.9x FP8 because of extra decode overheads + KV rebuilds. GPTQ sits between 0.7–0.85x depending on sequence length.
Aj Patel: Interesting. So AWQ is best for serving long-conversation workloads with high cache locality; FP8 is more stable for unpredictable prompt space.
Sam Ortiz: Any sign of regression on structured outputs or function-calling? those are sensitive to small token shifts.
Mia Chen: We ran 3 structured-output tests: json-schema, tool-call emulation, and code-gen unit tests. FP8 passed all baseline assertions. AWQ failed 2/30 random seeds on json-field-order (minor) and 3/100 on tool-call arg formatting — small but visible. GPTQ had 5/100 failures on code formatting.
Nina Green: Did you try hybrid routing (AWQ for NL intents, FP8 for code-heavy routes)?
Mia Chen: Yes — simulated smart routing: caller-level intent classifier routes to model variant. Effective strategy: use AWQ for NLU/chat routes (70% traffic), FP8 for codegen endpoints (30%). Results: overall p95 latency ~155ms, cost 0.72x baseline, and combined regressions dropped to near-zero because code kept on FP8.
Sam Ortiz: Ops question — are there runtime config knobs that reduce AWQ cold-start KV overhead? like prewarming or aggressive KV shard retention?
Mia Chen: Two levers helped: 1) prewarm with a 2-5s short-sequence warmup job on slot allocation; 2) increase KV cache retention TTL from 5m→20m for dedicated pools. Both lowered cold-start p95 by ~40ms.
ops-bot: Note: prewarm job triggers billing. Make sure to include in capacity cost calculations. :warning:
Aj Patel: For canary/deploys — recommend running A/B for at least 24h with synthetic low-hit-rate bursts to catch regressions where AWQ underperforms.
Mia Chen: Agreed. I'm going to push a small doc to eng-ml/bench-notes with full csvs and per-prompt diffs. Quick link placeholder: <https://redwood-internal/bench/1761005234-awq-fp8-gptq-70b>
Nina Green: Thanks! If someone can validate the hybrid routing probe with traffic replay, I can draft recommended deployment profiles (dedicated pool sizes, TTLs, routing thresholds).
Sam Ortiz: I'll take traffic replay tonight and tag results. Thanks for the runup, Mia. :thumbsup:
